name: Magenta-throated Woodstar
rangeDescription: Highlands of northern costa rica and western panama
description: Tiny hummingbird with long tail often cocked up. Slow bumblebee-like flight.

name: Henderson Island Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Henderson island (central pitcairn group, southeastern polynesia)
description: Relatively subdued in coloration for a fruit-dove. Has a dusky gray chest and face, a yellow eye-ring, a magenta forehead patch, and mostly green wings and body.

name: Bornean Wren-Babbler
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed lowlands of borneo
description: Large, stout wren-babbler. Highly dependent on pristine lowland forests; populations now declining and increasingly fragmented across Borneo as that habitat is rapidly deforested.

name: Eye-ringed Thistletail
rangeDescription: Andes of central peru (junín)
description: Well-named bird found only in a small area of the eastern Andes in central Peru. Like other thistletails, it is gray and brown with a long, wispy tail and an orange chin.

name: Short-tailed Woodstar
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of southwestern ecuador and northwestern peru
description: Tiny hummingbird with a very short tail found in arid scrub and desert in western Ecuador and northwestern Peru. Male has glittering violet “beard” that is bordered by white above and below.

name: Sri Lanka Myna
rangeDescription: Humid forest of sri lanka
description: Rotund, medium-sized black starling with yellow wattles on the nape, a stout, bicolored bill, and white flashes in the wing. Typically in small groups in the canopy of hill forest, and nearby gardens and woods.

name: Red-necked Amazon
rangeDescription: Montane forest of dominica (lesser antilles)
description: A chunky and gregarious resident of wet upland forests; often found in flocks of up to 15 birds. Its green body, bluish head, and orange-red spot on upper chest readily separates this species from the Imperial Parrot, the only other parrot sharing its range, as well as parrot species commonly kept in captivity.

name: Malabar Barbet
rangeDescription: Southwestern india (goa southward to kerala and western tamil nadu)
description: A chunky green barbet with diagnostic red over its entire face, forehead, throat, and breast. It has a diffuse blue band on the sides of the head and breast, while a thick black traverse band separates the blue parts from the red.

name: White-crowned Shama
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northern borneo, including labuan, balembangan, and banggi islands (off northeastern borneo)
description: Black with an orange belly and bright white crown; also note white rump and undertail. Endemic to northern Borneo, where it inhabits lowland and foothill forests, including swamps and around streams.

name: Clarion Wren
rangeDescription: Clarion island (revillagigedo islands off western mexico)
description: This wren is found only on Clarión Island, which is located in the Pacific Ocean about 450 miles southwest of the tip of Baja California in Mexico. It is warm brown with slightly paler underparts, bars on the wings and tail, faint streaks on the face, and a pale eyering.

name: White-collared Starling
rangeDescription: Cameroon to gabon, central african republic, and northern democratic republic of the congo
description: The male is an unusual and beautiful starling that is glossy blue-black with a broad white collar. Females are duller, gray with paler mottling on the underparts.

name: Purple-breasted Sunbird
rangeDescription: Montane forest of eastern democratic republic of the congo, western uganda, rwanda, and burundi
description: Long, slim medium-sized sunbird. Breeding males show an array of beautiful iridescent colors in good light, and have a very long, thin tail year-round.

name: Buff-throated Tody-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Foothills on east slope of andes in ecuador, peru, and western bolivia
description: Small and rather scarce flycatcher found inside tall, undisturbed cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes. Note olive back and wings, buffy head and breast, and pale gray belly.

name: Spix's Macaw
rangeDescription: Palm groves of northeastern brazil (northern bahia); on verge of extinction
description: Now declared extinct in the wild; only a few individuals survive in captivity. Medium-sized macaw with grayish head shading to deep glaucous blue in the rest of the plumage, contrasting with the black sturdy bill.

name: Crowned Cormorant
rangeDescription: Coastal southwestern africa (angola to south africa)
description: A small, plain-backed cormorant that is restricted to near-shore marine environments, where it is uncommon. Sometimes it occurs in coastal estuaries alongside the similar Long-tailed Cormorant, which has a shorter crest (year-round), a pale-speckled back, and a relatively longer tail.

name: White-rumped Monjita
rangeDescription: Savanna and campos of eastern brazil, northeastern paraguay, and eastern bolivia
description: Large flycatcher of savannas with scattered trees close to water. White below with a white head, rump, and uppertail.

name: Huambo Cisticola
rangeDescription: West-central angola
description: Large, plain, long-tailed cisticola with a rufous cap, gray-brown back, and pale whitish underparts. Found in open habitats with grass and small trees, often in rugged and mountainous areas.

name: Gray's Grasshopper Warbler
rangeDescription: Northeastern asia; winters to philippines, indonesia, and western new guinea
description: An odd, thrush-like warbler; extremely shy and seldom seen as it lurks about in dense undergrowth. The largest grasshopper-warbler, with a distinctly robust appearance.

name: Parrot Crossbill
rangeDescription: Coniferous forest of northeastern europe to western siberia
description: Bull-necked, big-headed crossbill with a deep and heavy bill, otherwise identical to Red Crossbill. Males are red; females and juveniles greenish.

name: Northern Gannet
rangeDescription: Breeds north atlantic coasts; ranges to coastal northwestern africa
description: Large seabird of the Atlantic with long, pointed bill, wings, and tail. Adults bright white with cream-colored head and black wingtips.
